question: The number of prime numbers lying between 331 and 345, both included, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

List possible prime candidates by avoiding even numbers and multiples of 5: 331, 333, 337, 339, 341, 343.

Eliminate multiples of 3 (sum of digits is divisible by 3): 333 and 339 are removed.

Check the remaining against primes up to √345 ≈ 18 (7, 11, 13, 17).

341 = 11 × 31 and 343 = 7 × 49, so both are not prime.

The remaining numbers 331 and 337 are prime, giving a total of 2 numbers.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 prime numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The range of numbers is from 331 to 345 (both included).

**Method to find prime numbers:**

A number is prime if it is greater than 1 and has no divisors other than 1 and itself.

⇒ Total numbers in the range: 331, 332, 333, 334, 335, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 342, 343, 344, 345.

⇒ Eliminate all even numbers: 331, 333, 335, 337, 339, 341, 343, 345.

⇒ Eliminate multiples of 5 (ending in 5): 331, 333, 337, 339, 341, 343.

⇒ Eliminate multiples of 3 (sum of digits ÷ 3): 333 (sum = 9) and 339 (sum = 15).

⇒ Remaining candidates: 331, 337, 341, 343.

⇒ Check divisibility by other primes (7, 11, 13, 17) up to √345 ≈ 18:

⇒ 341 ÷ 11 = 31 (Not prime)

⇒ 343 ÷ 7 = 49 (Not prime)

⇒ 331 and 337 are not divisible by any prime ≤ 18, so they are prime numbers.

⇒ Total number of prime numbers = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 prime numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a positive integer greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct divisors: 1 and itself.

Primality Test Shortcut

To check if a number N is prime, we only need to test its divisibility by all prime numbers less than or equal to √N.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime or mutually prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 1. They do not necessarily have to be prime numbers.

Twin Primes

Twin primes are a pair of prime numbers that have a difference of 2 (e.g., 11 and 13, or 41 and 43).
